Neha / Monica,

Attached is a draft we can drop into their SIG template: SIG_BCDR_answers_v1.xlsx. Key excerpts below you can paste into the SIG where appropriate. I marked items that differ for Private deployments.

- Service classification / RTO / RPO (hosted):
  - Control plane (API management, auth): RTO = 5 minutes (failover via active-passive regional control plane), RPO = 0 (stateless control plane with replicated metadata stores).
  - Inference endpoints (stateless model serving): RTO = 2–5 minutes with automated routing to warm standby clusters in an alternate region; RPO = near-zero for request routing (no customer data persisted), model artifacts are replicated and versioned with RPO = 1 hour for model registry sync during active deployments.
  - Long-running jobs / batch inference: RTO = 30 minutes (job restart/resubmit workflows), RPO = up to 1 hour depending on checkpointing cadence.

- Backups & retention:
  - Customer artifacts (configs, workspace metadata): continuous snapshots with incremental backups to encrypted S3; retention 90 days for standard customers, configurable to longer retention under contract.
  - Model artifacts and registries: periodic snapshots + Git-backed versioning; primary snapshots retained 365 days, cold archives retained per contract.
  - Audit & telemetry logs: indexed logging retained 180 days in our hosted plan (can be extended), with immutable archival for compliance engagements.
  - All backups are encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS integration available for Dedicated/Private customers.

- Cross-region failover / architecture:
  - Hosted: Multi-AZ deployments in primary region with warm-standby region(s). We use DNS-based weighted routing + health checks and automated orchestration to shift traffic to the standby cluster. The failover process is automated for control plane incidents; for model-serving capacity events we rely on autoscaling + fallback to lower-cost model variants as a temporary mitigation.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): Failover strategy depends on customer topology; we provide runbooks and automation hooks but the customer owns network peering and any cross-region replication unless we operate a managed private control plane under contract.

- DR testing / evidence:
  - Last full DR exercise (hosted) — 2025-10-09 (tabletop + live failover simulation to secondary region; objectives met).
  - Quarterly tabletop exercises + annual live failover test.
  - Runbooks, playbooks, recorded test reports available on request (redacted versions included in attached network-diagram-2026-01.pdf and the runbook link).

- Additional notes / limitations:
  - RTO guarantees in contract (SLA) are available for Dedicated customers under reserved capacity agreements; hosted customers get best-effort with published targets and incident rollback policies.
  - For Private on-prem, RTO/RPO commitments require runway to install managed agents and replication config; we flag clearance items in the SIG.

I attached: SIG_BCDR_answers_v1.xlsx (SIG-aligned responses) and network-diagram-2026-01.pdf (regional architecture snapshot). Mark any answers you want softened for procurement.

-David

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is our completed SIG BCDR section (SIG_BCDR_answers_v1.xlsx) and a regional architecture snapshot (network-diagram-2026-01.pdf).

Highlights (summary of attachments):
- RTO: Control plane 5 min, inference endpoints 2–5 min failover to warm standby; batch jobs 30 min; see attached spreadsheet for per-component rows.
- RPO: Near-zero for request routing; model artifact replication RPO ~1 hour; backups and logs retention per table.
- Backups: Encrypted incremental snapshots to S3 with cross-region replication; retention configurable by contract.
- Failover: Hosted uses automated DNS + orchestration to shift traffic to warm standby region(s); Private deployments require customer-managed networking and we supply runbooks.
- Evidence: last full live failover test 2025-10-09; quarterly tabletop exercises and annual live drills. Runbook excerpts included.
